title: Mona Lisa
description: The Mona Lisa is a half-length portrait painting by Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci. It has been called 'the best known, the most visited, the most written about, the most sung about, the most parodied work of art in the world.' The painting is thought to be a portrait of Lisa Gherardini, the wife of a Florentine merchant Francesco del Giocondo.
creditLine: Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain.

title: The Birth of Venus
description: The Birth of Venus depicts the goddess Venus emerging from the sea as a fully grown woman. The painting is in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence and is one of the most celebrated works of the Early Renaissance. Botticelli drew on classical mythology and Neoplatonic philosophy for this masterpiece commissioned by the Medici family.

title: The Creation of Adam
description: The Creation of Adam is a fresco painting by Michelangelo, forming part of the Sistine Chapel ceiling. It illustrates the Biblical creation narrative from Genesis in which God gives life to Adam, the first man. The iconic image of the near-touching hands of God and Adam has become one of the most replicated images in history.

title: The School of Athens
description: The School of Athens is a fresco by the Italian Renaissance artist Raphael. It was painted between 1509 and 1511. The work groups the greatest philosophers and scientists of antiquity around the central figures of Plato and Aristotle. Several figures in the painting are portraits of Renaissance contemporaries, including Leonardo da Vinci as Plato.

title: Vitruvian Man
description: The Vitruvian Man is a drawing made by Leonardo da Vinci around 1490. It is accompanied by notes based on the work of the architect Vitruvius. The drawing depicts a man in two superimposed positions with his arms and legs apart. It represents Leonardo's study of the ideal human proportions and the relationship between human body and geometry.

title: David
description: David is a masterpiece of Renaissance sculpture created from 1501 to 1504 by Michelangelo. It is a marble statue of the Biblical figure David, a favoured subject in the art of Florence. Standing at 5.17 metres, the statue represents the ideal of Renaissance humanism and the beauty of the male form, having become one of the most recognised works of Renaissance art.

title: The Last Supper
medium: Tempera on gesso, pitch and mastic
description: The Last Supper is a mural painting by Leonardo da Vinci housed in the refectory of the Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie in Milan. The work represents the scene of The Last Supper as told in the Gospel of John, specifically the moment Jesus announces that one of the twelve will betray him.
creditLine: Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan. Public domain.

title: Primavera
description: Primavera, also known as Allegory of Spring, is a large panel painting in tempera paint. It has been described as 'one of the most written about, and contested, paintings in the world'. The nine figures in the work are generally identified as mythological characters from classical antiquity: Mercury, the Three Graces, Venus, Cupid, Flora, Chloris, and Zephyrus.

title: Sistine Madonna
description: Sistine Madonna, also called the Madonna di San Sisto, is an oil painting by the Italian artist Raphael. Commissioned by Pope Julius II for the church of San Sisto in Piacenza, it shows the Virgin Mary holding the Christ child with Saint Sixtus on her left and Saint Barbara on her right. The two cherubs (putti) at the bottom of the picture have become one of the most reproduced images in the world.
creditLine: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden. Public domain.

title: Self-portrait at Twenty-Eight
description: Self-portrait at the Age of Twenty-Eight is an oil painting by the German Renaissance master Albrecht Dürer. Painted in 1500, it is one of the most significant self-portraits in the history of art. By arranging his figure in a frontal pose previously reserved for images of Christ, Dürer proposed an elevated status for the Renaissance artist as a divinely-inspired creator.

title: Portrait of a Young Woman (Simonetta Vespucci)
description: This striking portrait is thought to depict Simonetta Vespucci, the Florentine noblewoman and great beauty who was the object of admiration by Giuliano de' Medici. The profile portraiture style was common in the 15th century and derived from Roman coins and medals. The elaborate coiffure and mythological serpent motif suggest this may be an idealized allegorical portrait.

title: Venus of Urbino
description: Venus of Urbino is an oil painting by the Italian master Titian. It depicts a nude young woman, traditionally interpreted as the goddess Venus, reclining on a couch or bed in an intimate interior. The painting was commissioned by Guidobaldo della Rovere, later Duke of Urbino. It was groundbreaking in its frank and sensual depiction of the nude female form.

title: The Arnolfini Portrait
description: The Arnolfini Portrait is an oil painting by Early Netherlandish painter Jan van Eyck. It is a full-length double portrait depicting Giovanni di Nicolao di Arnolfini and his wife in a lavishly furnished interior. The painting is one of the most original and complex paintings in Western art history, famous for its technical mastery and the mysteries of its symbolism.

title: Assumption of the Virgin
description: Assumption of the Virgin is a Renaissance painting by Titian. It is the largest altarpiece in Venice and one of the most celebrated religious paintings of the Renaissance. The work depicts the Virgin Mary ascending to heaven surrounded by clouds and angels, with the apostles watching from below and God the Father waiting above.
creditLine: Basilica di Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari, Venice. Public domain.

title: Young Hare
description: Young Hare is a masterwork of observational study by German Renaissance master Albrecht Dürer. Executed in watercolour and gouache, it captures with extraordinary naturalism the texture of the fur and the alert poise of the animal. The work exemplifies the Renaissance interest in close observation of nature and scientific accuracy in art.

title: Portrait of Baldassare Castiglione
description: This portrait depicts the Italian diplomat and writer Baldassare Castiglione, author of The Book of the Courtier. One of the most celebrated portraits of the Renaissance, it combines psychological depth with a supremely elegant pose. The soft grey and black palette and three-quarter view were highly influential and were copied by Rembrandt and Rubens.
creditLine: Musée du Louvre, Paris. Public domain.

title: The Madonna of the Meadow
description: The Madonna of the Meadow shows the Virgin Mary with the infant Jesus and St. John the Baptist in an open Umbrian landscape. The pyramidal composition groups the three figures in a stable, serene harmony — a hallmark of Raphael's High Renaissance style. The graceful triangular arrangement became immensely influential in Western religious painting.

title: Bacchus
description: Bacchus is an early marble sculpture by Michelangelo created when the artist was just 22 years old. It depicts the Roman god of wine in a state of intoxication, with a small satyr stealing grapes behind him. The swaying, unsteady pose brilliantly conveys drunkenness — an unprecedented naturalism for a free-standing sculpture of this period.
creditLine: Bargello National Museum, Florence. Public domain.

title: Lady with an Ermine
description: Lady with an Ermine is a painting by Leonardo da Vinci. The sitter is generally identified as Cecilia Gallerani, who was the mistress of Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan, when Leonardo was in his service. The portrait is remarkable for its lifelike quality and the psychological depth conveyed through the subtle turn of the sitter's head and her gaze directed off-canvas.

title: Portrait of Pope Julius II
description: This portrait of Pope Julius II is considered one of the greatest portraits of the Renaissance. The pope sits in a three-quarter pose in his pontifical chair, looking downward in meditation or dejection. The work established a format for papal portraiture that influenced portrait painting for generations. Julius II was a major patron who commissioned the Sistine Chapel ceiling and St. Peter's Basilica.

title: The Four Apostles
description: The Four Apostles is a pair of paintings by Albrecht Dürer, considered his artistic testament. The two panels depict Saints John, Peter, Mark, and Paul as embodiments of the four temperaments (sanguine, phlegmatic, choleric, and melancholic). Dürer donated them to the city of Nuremberg, and they represent the culmination of his mastery of oil painting and his reformist Lutheran faith.

title: Pietà
description: The Pietà is a work of Renaissance sculpture by Michelangelo, housed in St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City. It is the first of several works of the same theme by the artist. Considered one of the greatest works of sculpture, the scene depicts the Virgin Mary cradling the body of Jesus Christ after the Crucifixion. Michelangelo was only 24 when he completed it.
creditLine: St. Peter's Basilica, Vatican. Public domain.

title: Portrait of a Man (Self-Portrait?)
description: Often interpreted as a self-portrait, this small painting is among the earliest surviving examples of Western portraiture. The sitter wears a chaperon, a fashionable twisted headdress. The inscription on the frame reads 'Als Ich Kan' (the best I can do), a phrase Van Eyck used as a personal motto. The lifelike gaze and intense realism mark a turning point in Western art.

title: Melencolia I
description: Melencolia I is a large engraving by the German Renaissance master Albrecht Dürer, enigmatic and rich in symbolism. A winged figure sits in melancholy surrounded by the tools of geometry and craftsmanship — a putto, an hourglass, scales, a magic square, a sphere, and a polyhedron. It is considered one of the most complex engravings ever made and has been the subject of centuries of scholarly analysis.
creditLine: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York. Public domain.

title: Baptism of Christ
description: The Baptism of Christ is a painting begun by Andrea del Verrocchio in which Leonardo da Vinci participated. According to Vasari, Leonardo painted the leftmost angel, which far surpassed Verrocchio's own work in quality. The angel's grace and the atmospheric landscape of the background are believed to be Leonardo's contributions to the work.

title: Portrait of Ginevra de' Benci
description: Portrait of Ginevra de' Benci is the only painting by Leonardo da Vinci in the Americas. It depicts the young Florentine noblewoman Ginevra de' Benci against an unusual translucent juniper tree — a visual pun on her name (ginepro = juniper). It is Leonardo's earliest surviving portrait and one of the first three-quarter portraits in Italian painting.
creditLine: National Gallery of Art, Washington D.C. Public domain.

title: The Temptation of St. Anthony
description: The Temptation of St. Anthony is Michelangelo's earliest known painting, made when he was around 12 or 13 years old. The composition is copied from an engraving by the German Martin Schongauer, but Michelangelo reportedly went to the fish market to study the scales and fins of strange sea-creatures to paint the demons with greater naturalism.
creditLine: Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth. Public domain.

title: Ghent Altarpiece (The Adoration of the Mystic Lamb)
description: The Ghent Altarpiece is a large and complex polyptych altarpiece painted by Hubert and Jan van Eyck. Completed in 1432, it is one of the oldest and most famous surviving oil paintings in the world. The work contains 12 panels and depicts the heavenly landscape on the upper register and the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb below, representing the redemption of humanity.
creditLine: St. Bavo's Cathedral, Ghent. Public domain.

title: Portrait of Doge Leonardo Loredan
description: This celebrated portrait depicts Leonardo Loredan, who served as the 75th Doge of Venice from 1501 to 1521. Bellini's penetrating characterisation, with the Doge's subtle likeness captured in an almost sculptural three-quarter pose, influenced portrait painting across Europe. The shimmering brocade of the Doge's robe and the pure blue background are rendered with exceptional skill.

title: The Ambassadors
description: The Ambassadors is a double portrait by the German painter Hans Holbein the Younger. Two young men stand either side of a table loaded with objects symbolic of their learning and worldly accomplishments. Famously difficult to interpret, the work features a large anamorphic skull in the foreground — a memento mori visible only from an extreme side angle.
